cards.title: Litter and public spaces
facts: Litter blocks drains and causes waterlogging in the monsoon.
People copy what they see others do, good or bad.
do: Keep the wrapper until you find a bin
Politely encourage friends to do the same
dont: Don't drop litter even if others do
Don't throw things out of vehicle windows

myths.statement: One wrapper doesn't matter; it's the city's job to clean up.
myths.truth: Millions of 'just one wrapper' block drains. Everyone shares the job.

quiz.q: There's no dustbin on the bus. What do you do with your wrapper?
options: Throw it out of the window
Keep it in your bag until you find a bin
quiz.explanation: Fold it into your bag and bin it later.

situations: {name} finishes a packet of chips {at}. There's no dustbin anywhere, and {relation} says 'Just drop it under the seat, everyone does.'
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.point: Keep the wrapper until finding a bin
rubric.note: Fold it into a pocket or bag and bin it later.

rubric.point: Don't drop it, even if 'everyone does'
rubric.note: The right thing doesn't depend on others.

cards.title: Queues and public transport
facts: Letting people off first makes boarding faster for everyone.
Priority seats are for elderly, pregnant, disabled people and parents with small children.
do: Wait your turn in the queue
Let passengers get off before boarding
Offer your seat to someone who needs it more
dont: Don't push or cut the queue
Don't play loud music without headphones

myths.statement: Priority seats are only for people who ask for them.
myths.truth: Offer them without being asked. Many people won't ask.

quiz.q: The metro doors open and the train is crowded. What first?
quiz.explanation: Letting people off first makes boarding faster for everyone.

situations: {name} has just got the last seat on a crowded bus. At the next stop, an elderly woman with a heavy bag gets on and holds the rail. {relation} whispers 'Pretend you're asleep.'
scenario.question: What should {name} do?

rubric.note: Offer without waiting to be asked.

rubric.point: Help with the bag if she wants
rubric.note: Small help goes a long way.

rubric.point: Not pretend to sleep / set a good example

cards.title: Finding a lost child
facts: Lost children should be handed to officials such as security, police or staff, not taken home.
1098 is CHILDLINE, India's free helpline for children in need.
do: Stay with the child in a busy, visible place
Tell security, a shop counter or police
dont: Don't take the child home or away from the area

myths.statement: If you find a lost child, it's best to take them home and look after them.
myths.truth: Hand them to security, staff or police at the spot, where parents will search.

quiz.q: You find a crying child alone in a mall. Best step?
options: Stay with them and tell security or staff
quiz.explanation: Staff can make announcements, and parents will come back to that area.

cards.title: Caring for public property
facts: Public property is paid for by everyone's taxes.
Leaking public taps can waste thousands of litres.
do: Report damage or leaks to the authority or school
Use walls and benches as they're meant to be used
dont: Don't scribble on walls or monuments
Don't damage benches, signs or plants

myths.statement: Writing your name on a monument is harmless fun.
myths.truth: It damages heritage that belongs to everyone, and it's an offence.

quiz.q: You see a public tap left running. What do you do?
options: Close it, and report it if it's broken
quiz.explanation: Close it and report broken taps so they get fixed.
